ev.q: In 2017, 7.1% met fruit intake recommendations, and 2.0% met vegetable intake recommendations.
CDC analyzed data from the 2017 national and state Youth Risk Behavior Surveys
7.1% of high school students met federal intake recommendations for fruits
Nationally, 7.1% of high school students met federal intake recommendations for fruits
the percentage of students meeting recommendations for fruit consumption was higher among males (9.7%) than among females (4.7%)
State-specific estimates ranged from 4.0% (Connecticut) to 9.3% (Louisiana) for fruits
CDC conducts the national YRBS biennially and uses a three-stage cluster sample design
The Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System monitors prevalence of youth health behaviors

methods_quotes.q: Balanced repeated replication, replicate weights, and Taylor linearization were used to calculate 95% CIs for the percentage meeting recommendations
were used to predict whether students met recommendations for their age and sex based on the number of times per day
T-tests were used to examine statistical differences by demographics (p-value <0.05).
For vegetables, given CIs that include zero, only upper bounds are shown.
Analyses were performed using SAS (version 9.4; SAS Institute) survey procedures to account for complex sampling designs
Dashes indicate that estimates in states where the sample size was <100 were considered unstable and were not reported.
